## Customise and extend report modules

`camtrapReport` builds ecological reports from reusable **modules** containing narrative text, analyses, tables, and figures. This guide shows how to inspect, create, register, test, and manage modules. Explore the [Module Catalog](module-catalog.html) before developing a new one.

> **Important:** Work with a copy of the module registry in a writable project directory, not the installed package. Modules execute R code, so use only trusted sources.

```{r module-workflow, echo=FALSE, out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 1. Modular workflow for defining, registering, selecting, and running report modules in *camtrapReport*.", fig.alt="Modular workflow for defining, registering, selecting, and running report modules in camtrapReport."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/modular-design.png")
```

### 1. Explore available modules

```{r list-existing-modules, eval=FALSE}
# List all available modules
list_Modules()

# Show all section names used in the report
section_names()
```

### 2. Create a YAML module

A YAML module specifies its identifier, title, parent section, narrative, and code. Figure 2 illustrates how these elements appear in the report.

```{r yaml-module-structure, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 2. Relationship between the main components of a YAML report module and its output in the Ecological Report.", fig.alt="Diagram showing how the main components of a YAML report module correspond to the heading, explanatory text, and analytical output in the Ecological Report."}
knitr::include_graphics(
  "figures/YAML_Module_to_EcologicalReport.png"
)
```

Save the following example as `species_table.yml` in your project directory. It uses the species table stored in `cm$data_status`; inspect that object before adapting the example to another dataset.

~~~yaml
name: species_table
title: "Species summary table"
parent: "results"
text: "This section provides a summary of the species detected in the camera-trap dataset, including their taxonomy and total number of captures."

code: |
  #| echo: false
  #| message: false
  #| warning: false

  species_table <- object$data_status$Species$Table

  if (!is.null(species_table) && nrow(species_table) > 0) {
    knitr::kable(
      species_table,
      caption = "Species detected in the camera-trap dataset."
    )
  } else {
    cat("No species table is available for this dataset.")
  }
~~~

### 3. Register the module

Copy the bundled registry to a writable location and register the YAML file there. The example inserts the module before `richness`.

```{r add-new-module, eval=FALSE}
# Create a writable project-level module registry once
bundled_modules <- system.file(
  "reportSections",
  package = "camtrapReport"
)
module_dir <- here::here("reportSections")

if (!dir.exists(module_dir)) {
  dir.create(module_dir)
  file.copy(
    list.files(bundled_modules, full.names = TRUE),
    module_dir,
    recursive = TRUE
  )
}

# Add a new module from a YAML file
added <- add_Module(
  x = "species_table.yml",
  before = "richness",
  test = FALSE,
  object = cm,
  dir = module_dir
)

# Check whether the module has been added
list_Modules(dir = module_dir)
```

### 4. Add and test the module

Add the registered module to the active `camReport` object, test it independently, then generate the complete report.

```{r update-current-object, eval=FALSE}
cm$addReportObject(added$module)
listReportSections(cm)
```

```{r test-new-module, eval=FALSE}
# Test the new module only
testSection(
  added$module,
  object = cm,
  view = TRUE
)
```

```{r generate-report-with-new-module, eval=FALSE}
# Generate the full report
report(cm, view = TRUE)
```

Check the output for errors, missing figures, duplicated headings, and scientific accuracy. Module-specific dependencies should be declared in the YAML; `install_all()` can install missing optional packages when needed.

### Edit, reorder, or remove modules

To customise an existing module, edit a **project-level copy** of its YAML file and test the revised version. Report narratives can combine module templates, dataset metadata, and computed results; review them before publication.

```{r manage-existing-modules, eval=FALSE}
# Validate active module definitions and inspect the hierarchy
list_Modules(validate = TRUE, dir = module_dir)

# Move a module within the report hierarchy
move_Module(
  "species_table",
  after = "captures",
  parent = "results",
  dir = module_dir
)

# Move a module and its children to the module trash
remove_Module("species_table", recursive = TRUE, dir = module_dir)

# Inspect active and deleted modules
list_Modules(include_trash = TRUE, dir = module_dir)

# Restore a removed module
restore_Module("species_table", test = TRUE, dir = module_dir)
```

Removed modules can be restored from the registry's trash. `empty_trash()` permanently deletes them, so retain backups before using it. After changes, refresh the report object's configuration and verify its sections and rendered output.

### Reproducibility and further guidance

Keep the input data, customised YAML files, relevant dependencies, analytical settings, and package versions together. Test modules against missing or empty data and check method-specific assumptions before sharing results.

For reusable module selections, see [Analytical Profiles](profiles.html). For end-to-end report configuration, see the [Ecological Report guide](ecological-report.html).
